note: This night reads two source tarballs and two web pages. No third-party bytes are committed: PostgreSQL's source is redistributable under its licence, but nothing here needs it in the repository -- every measurement is re-derivable by fetching the tarball, comparing the SHA-256 below, and running the four scripts in this directory. The hashes were verified against the publisher's own .sha256 files, which are listed as separate entries because a hash a night computes for itself proves only that the night did not change the file.

sources.licence: The PostgreSQL Licence (see COPYRIGHT in the tarball) permits redistribution; not committed because the manifest is the better warrant and the file is 22 MB

sources.what: the publisher's own SHA-256 for the above
sources.why: so the population is identified by the publisher's hash and not only by this night's

sources.what: the publisher's own SHA-256 for the above
PostgreSQL 18 manual, Appendix A. PostgreSQL Error Codes -- the published face of the vocabulary
sources.why: an independent check on the tarball's generator: the manual shows 262 SQLSTATE literals, and the tarball's doc/src/sgml/generate-errcodes-table.pl emits exactly one row per code carrying a condition name -- 268 codes minus the 6 without one. The two agree exactly, which is what licenses the claim that every siteless code is nevertheless in the published manual.

sources.what: the publisher's source directory listing, used to establish that 18.6 is the newest release on 2026-09-01

files_inside_the_tarball_that_the_argume.role: THE VOCABULARY -- 268 codes in 43 classes; its header comment documents the format and states that where the optional fourth field is absent 'the PL/pgSQL condition and the SGML entry will not be generated'
generates Appendix A; skips every line without a condition name ('next unless defined($condition_name)')
generates PL/pgSQL's condition-name table; skips warnings and success ('next unless $type eq \'E\'') as well as lines without a condition name
plpgsql_recognize_err_condition -- converts any five-character [0-9A-Z] string straight to a SQLSTATE with MAKE_SQLSTATE, before consulting the condition-name table at all
RAISE ... USING ERRCODE = '<literal>' -- accepts any five-character [0-9A-Z] string, in or out of the vocabulary
the embedded-SQL client's own SQLSTATE constants, defined as string literals rather than as the published macros -- the route rule C exists to find
the two non-canonical imposition sites read by hand: the default code for a sub-WARNING message (line 454) and errcode_for_file_access's errno mapping (line 932)
